articles.title: Ebola virus behind massive outbreak in DRC could be mutating, officials say
articles.excerpt: The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.The Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, was first reported on 15 May, although there are suspicions the disease could have been spreading since January.There have been 3,973 cases and 1,801 deaths recorded as of 4 August, according to the DRC’s national public health institute. Speaking on Thursday, Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), told a press briefing cases had topped 4,000.The outbreak is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. There are eight times more cases, and six times more deaths than were recorded 11 weeks into the West Africa Ebola outbreak in 2014-18, which infected more than 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000.Kaseya said he had spoken to the director general of the World Health Organization, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and they planned studies “to check if there is no additional issue, or maybe if the virus is not mutating. Because the level of severity of this Bundibugyo outbreak is unprecedented.”More than two-thirds of Ebola deaths are happening in the community rather than in treatment centres. In a treatment centre run by MSF in Bunia, the capital of Ituri province, 90% of admitted patients do not appear on authorities’ lists of contacts of known cases. Both factors indicate high levels of untracked transmission.Kaseya said contact tracing in the DRC was insufficient, with only 10 contacts identified for every Ebola patient, when about 40 would be the expected number.Ebola is a viral haemorrhagic fever that can cause vomiting, diarrhoea, organ damage and internal bleeding.

articles.title: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
articles.excerpt: The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China.The US Congress has been served notice of the impending closures, which are being justified on cost grounds and follow a reassessment of the US’s bilateral relationships with a range of countries since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025.According to a notice served to several congressional committees, missions will close in St George’s, Grenada; Nagoya, Japan; Medan, Indonesia; Douala, Cameroon; and Winnipeg, Canada.The closures will continue a process of cutbacks in US state department operations overseen by Marco Rubio, the secretary of state. Last year, the department fired more than 1,300 employees, including 246 foreign services officers and 1,107 civil servants.More than half of the US’s 195 ambassadorial posts around the world remain unfilled, including in keys locations such as Germany, Cuba, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, according to the American Foreign Service Association.Democrats have criticized the latest planned closures, saying it risked leaving the field free for China.“China has a diplomatic presence in three of the five locations where the state department is closing shop and Beijing is going to exploit that new vacuum to undercut American interests,” said Jeanne Shaheen, the top Democrat on the Senate foreign relations committee.“The yearly operating costs of these diplomatic facilities represent a tiny fraction of the state department’s yearly budget,” Shaheen added.

articles.title: Top Ugandan footballer killed by robbers armed with paving stones
articles.excerpt: The Ugandan football community is in mourning after the death of a player who was fatally injured during a robbery in the capital, Kampala, on Tuesday night.David Owori, who captained Sports Club Villa, a Uganda Premier League club, and represented the national team, was attacked after resisting an attempt to steal his mobile phone and other belongings near his home in Makindye division.Racheal Kawala, a spokesperson for the Kampala Metropolitan police, said he was found unconscious by ​passersby, who took him to a nearby hospital. He was ​transferred to another hospital, where he was pronounced dead on Wednesday.Witnesses said attackers hit the footballer with paving stones before robbing him and fleeing, leaving him unconscious, the BBC reported.Owori, 27, was a right-back and midfielder for SC Villa. He helped the team win a record 17th Uganda Premier League title in 2024.He started his senior career in 2016 at the Uganda Premier League side Vipers Sports Club and had stints in Europe with Vélez CF in Spain and Utsiktens BK in Sweden.He played for the national team in the qualifiers for the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations.SC Villa said: “It is with profound sorrow that we announce the untimely passing of our captain, Owori, who had been receiving treatment at Case Clinic following an attack by suspected thugs. Our deepest condolences and prayers are with his family.”The Federation ​of Uganda Football Associations said: “David was not just a footballer. He was ​both a leader and an inspiration to a generation. As ​Captain of SC Villa, he led with courage, humility and passion. In the Uganda Cranes jersey, he carried the hopes of a nation.”It added: “We have lost a son, a leader and a star.

articles.title: Canadian government steps in as ‘out of control’ wildfires force thousands to flee
articles.excerpt: Canada’s federal government has announced it will provide urgent assistance to British Columbia after an onslaught of unprecedented fast-moving wildfires forced about 22,000 people to flee their homes in frantic evacuations.A total of 102 wildfires were raging across the province on Sunday, of which nearly half were categorised as “out of control”, according to the BC Wildfire Service. Of those fires, 78 ignited during the past week.The entire community of Summerland, about 30 miles south-west of the city of Kelowna and home to about 12,000 people, was evacuated overnight on Saturday, along with a further 8,000 people around nearby Peachland. About 10,000 others have been told to prepare to evacuate at a moment’s notice.“I approved a request for federal assistance from British Columbia to provide shelter and accommodations for people who have been forced to leave their homes,” said Eleanor Olszewski, Canada’s minister of emergency management and community resilience in a social media post on Sunday.“I have tasked federal officials, led by the government operations centre at Public Safety ‌Canada, to work with the province to ensure support reaches those who need it most,” she ​said.MapEfforts to battle the Bald Range wildfire have been hampered by the breakneck speed of its spread.The blaze was first detected late on Friday evening, and grew within hours to more than 40 sq miles (100 sq km) – nearly twice the size of the island of Manhattan – as it raced nearly nine miles toward Okanagan Lake.The province’s premier, David Eby, declared a state of emergency late on Saturday, telling reporters that the blaze had been “like a bomb going off.”Cliff Chapman, BC Wildfire Service’s director of provincial operations, said the prolonged hot and dry weather the province has faced this summer had resulted in “explosive” fire conditions never seen before.

articles.title: Costa Rican diplomat emerges as strong contender to be first female head of UN
articles.excerpt: A Costa Rican diplomat and former vice-president whose parents were refugees from the Holocaust has become the surprise frontrunner to lead the United Nations as its first female secretary general.Rebeca Grynspan, whose parents emigrated to Central America from Poland – and whose maternal grandparents were killed by the Nazis – is the current head of the UN conference on trade and development (UNCTAD), a body that has exhaustively tallied the economic damage inflicted by Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories.The current secretary general, António Guterres, will complete his second term on 31 December 2026 and under an informal system of regional rotation his successor is expected to come from Latin America.In a secret first straw poll of the UN security council, the five permanent and 10 temporary members were asked to say whether they supported, objected to or were neutral about each of seven candidates.Grynspan secured 10 “encourage” votes, four “no opinion” votes and one “discourage” vote. The identity of the discourage vote is not known, but the fact that she had only one objection places her in a strong opening position. The process is likely to conclude in October.Grynspan’s closest rival is Carolyn Rodrigues-Burkett, Guyana’s former UN envoy, with nine encourages, two discourages and four no opinions. At the close of a Bloomberg-sponsored debate at the general assembly last month she secured 49% of the vote among those attending, with Grynspan second on 14%.“Grynspan is seen by some as the continuity candidate, having the tacit support from Guterres,” said one western diplomat.

articles.title: ‘I couldn’t breathe’: the deadly health burden of wildfire smoke
articles.excerpt: A thousand kilometres from the infernos gorging on northern Ontario’s boreal forests, Erin O’Connor watched the sky above Canada’s biggest city turn an “almost post-apocalyptic” orange as it filled with light-scattering particles of soot and ash. Stepping outside the halls of Toronto General hospital, where air filters were keeping patients safe from the worst of the fumes, she was struck by a smell so strong it felt like standing by a campfire.“It really hit you in the face as soon as you walked outside,” said O’Connor, who runs University Health Network’s emergency department and saw a rise in patients presenting with allergies and shortness of breath. “As the days progressed, it was like that everywhere. It seemed even inside you could smell that burning.”Far more than the flames that have engulfed southern Europe and North America in recent weeks, it is the smoke that dominates the astonishing death toll from combusting nature. Thick with toxic gases that inflame the airways and tiny particulates that breach the lungs and ride the bloodstream to hit every organ in the body, fumes from landscape fires kill 1.5 million people each year, a study in the Lancet found in 2024 – more than floods, flames, storms and heat combined.So damaging are the lung-scarring effects of charred plant matter that people far from the fires may still perish. The plumes spewed by wildfires in Canada in 2023 caused 82,000 early deaths, a study in Nature found last year, with unfavourable winds pushing a third of the mortality burden into the US and another quarter into Europe. About 10% of the UK’s fine particulate pollution (PM2.5) comes from biomass burned abroad, researchers found in March.The Quilpituk Creek wildfire in British Columbia, seen here across Okanagan Lake. Photograph: Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press/APYet while scientists agree the health burden of wildfire smoke is jaw droppingly large, they are only beginning to untangle the complex links between exposure and mortality.

articles.title: US promises $1bn in security aid to Colombia as new rightwing president pledges drugs crackdown
articles.excerpt: The ​Trump administration plans to provide $1bn in security assistance to the ⁠government of Colombia’s new ​rightwing ‌president, the US state department announced, soon after Abelardo De La ‌Espriella was sworn in and used his inaugural speech to pledge a vigorous fight against drug trafficking, as well as austerity measures to restore confidence in the economy.De La Espriella, 48, won June’s runoff election with ⁠promises to crack down on armed groups, shrink ⁠the state by as much as 40% and ​revive the oil and gas sector.“I have come to close a long chapter of national resignation and, together with the people, embark on the most profound transformation ⁠of our destiny,” De La Espriella said at the Pichincha Battalion military base in Cali after being sworn in on Friday.“I send a firm message to the Colombian people: the time has come to restore order, authority and freedom,” said De La Espriella, who received the endorsement of Donald Trump before his runoff election.“Members of criminal gangs and narco-terrorist groups have two choices: submit to the ⁠rule of law or face the determined response of the Colombian state and its security forces,” the new president told assembled troops at the base during a 75-minute speech, adding the option of peace talks with armed groups had been “completely exhausted”.The US ⁠state department said in a statement on Friday: ⁠“As a cornerstone of this renewed partnership, the United States, working with Congress, ‌intends to announce $1 billion in assistance ​as part of a security package to support ⁠President de la Espriella’s ​Administration in ​achieving ​our shared goals.”De La Espriella’s ​election is part of a rightward shift rippling across Latin America.

articles.title: US police officer accused of killing three people in Mexico arrested at border
articles.excerpt: A Texas police officer has been arrested in Mexico after authorities there accused him of killing three people and critically injuring the mother of his child in what investigators say stemmed from a dispute over the custody of the minor.The Coahuila attorney general’s office said 35-year-old Chad Eberle was arrested on Wednesday at the border on a warrant accusing him of femicide and qualified homicide, according to La Razon de Mexico, a newspaper based in Mexico City. Under Mexican law, femicide refers to the intentional killing of a woman or girl because of her gender.According to La Razon, the deadly shooting happened in July in Saltillo, Mexico, after an argument over Eberle allegedly not having permission to take his three-year-old son. Two women and one man were killed in the attack.The victims were identified by La Razon with the first names and ages of Ana Laura, 44; Laura Jaquelín, 22; and Emanuel, 44. The child’s 26-year-old mother was also shot in the head and remained in critical condition, officials said.Investigators said Eberle was arrested while attempting to cross from Mexico into Texas through the international bridge at Piedras Negras, across from Eagle Pass, KTXS reported. Eberle had left the residence with his son in a gray Chevrolet Silverado, prompting investigators to launch a manhunt as they tracked the vehicle toward the Texas border, the US Sun reported.He was then intercepted before he could re-enter the US with the child. The three-year-old was unharmed and was later placed in the care of Coahuila’s child welfare agency.The San Antonio Express identified Eberle as a police officer in the central Texas town of Santa Anna.

articles.title: Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall in China as its strongest storm this year
articles.excerpt: Typhoon Dolphin, the most powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year, has made landfall on the country’s east coast, bringing torrential rain and strong ⁠winds and triggering warnings ​of flooding and landslides.The storm has already swept through Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.Dolphin made landfall near Yuhuan in Zhejiang province at about ⁠5:30pm (0930 GMT) on Sunday, China’s meteorological authorities said. It brought maximum sustained winds of 94mph (151 km/h) near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.In addition to evacuating at least 30,300 people, Shanghai has cancelled about 1,500 flights, according to the flight-tracking data provider VariFlight.A struggles against high winds and driving rain in Dongsha, Zhejiang province, as Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall. Photograph: Huang Zongzhi/Xinhua/APAuthorities moved offshore ⁠workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.Torrential ​rain is forecast for Monday across Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Fujian, ‌north-eastern Jiangxi, central and southern Anhui, and ‌much of Jiangsu.

articles.title: Chinese EV sales surge to new high in Europe putting tariffs under scrutiny
articles.excerpt: Chinese electric car sales have risen across Europe to a record high driven by strong demand and low tariffs in the UK and a surge in buyers in Italy.Against a backdrop of claims that Chinese carmakers are “dumping” state-subsidised vehicles in the EU and UK to gain market share, the figures will give impetus to calls for quotas and higher tariffs to protect European manufacturers.The share of electric cars sold by Chinese brands rose to 14.2% across western European markets – or one in every seven battery electric vehicles (BEVs) – in the first five months of this year, according to Schmidt Automotive Research. The 171,800 sales represented an increase in market share of nearly five percentage points versus the same period in 2025.Brands including BYD, Chery, SAIC and Xpeng have targeted Europe for exports, as the Chinese industry seeks to dominate the global electric vehicle market. This has put traditional European manufacturers under intense pressure when tougher emissions rules are forcing them to increase their own BEV sales.Chart showing how China has increased its market share in electric vehicle sales in Europe from 9.4% to 14.2% The increase in European sales comes despite EU tariffs of up to 35.3% for electric cars made by some Chinese manufacturers, on top of the standard 10% import duty.The UK is the largest European market for Chinese cars because the government has declined to follow the EU’s lead in imposing extra levies. The UK accounted for a quarter of Chinese BEV sales across the 18 biggest Western European markets.Although Italy accounted for a fifth of the total, Schmidt said this was an “anomaly”. One manufacturer, Leapmotor, sent thousands of its cheap T03 electric cars into the country to take advantage of purchase subsidies from the government.

articles.title: Thailand school shooting toll rises to nine after 12-year-old dies, police say
articles.excerpt: The death toll from a school shooting in Thailand rose to nine on Saturday, after police said a 12-year-old girl caught up in Friday’s incident had died.Police at the Plai Bang Police Station in Nonthaburi Province said the girl, who had been treated at hospital with critical wounds, had died, a day after a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot his grandparents and then killed more people at his school before turning the gun on ⁠himself.The 14-year-old wounded more than 30 people in the ⁠shooting at the Debsirin Nonthaburi school northwest of Bangkok. Fourteen people remained in hospital on Saturday evening, seven of them in critical condition.Police are questioning more witnesses as part of their investigation, including the suspect’s parents. The boy had lived with his grandparents for 12 years after his parents had separated, Atthapol Anusit, deputy commissioner of the Provincial Police Region 1, ‌told reporters on Sunday.The suspected attacker fired at least 26 bullets with a gun belonging to his grandfather, and was found with 34 additional ammunition rounds.Police on Sunday told reporters the teenager had an air ⁠gun confiscated by a teacher last year and had watched violent content online and used social media to learn how to ⁠use a firearm.“According to witness interviews, the perpetrator had begun showing interest in ​studying the use of firearms ‌for some time, about one ‌to two years,” Atthapol said.Atthapol, who said police had so far interviewed 17 witnesses, said a knife had also been found in the boy’s bag and other evidence found at the crime scenes included a firearm, spent cartridge cases, and a personal computer.On the day of the incident, the suspected shooter remained inside the school after reports of the attack emerged, Arsit Sampantharat, the permanent secretary of the interior ministry, told PPTV.A lockdown at the school was declared over in about half an hour.

articles.title: Thailand school shooting: eight killed including suspected attacker, police say
articles.excerpt: A Thai teenager killed his grandparents before opening fire at his school, where he shot five people dead and took his own life, police have said, in an attack that has shaken a country struggling to deal with gun violence.The 14-year-old wounded more than 30 people in the ⁠shooting at the prestigious Debsirin Nonthaburi school northwest of Bangkok. Nine people were in a critical condition, the Thai health department said.For Prompong Namwong, an English teacher at the school, it was a normal morning until a panicked student from another class flung open the door, trying to find somewhere to hide. In the corridor, Prompong heard other teachers shouting that there had been a mass shooting downstairs.Prompong Namwong. Photograph: Natasha MayWhen Prompong recounted the ordeal to the Guardian, he hesitated between calling the 14-year-old, whom he saw run in front of his classroom, “killer” or “student”.At that moment, “I thought I was going to die, for sure,” he said.The suspected attacker fired at least 26 bullets with a gun belonging to his grandfather, and was found with 34 additional ammunition rounds.Students seek safety during Thai school shooting – videoThe suspected shooter remained inside the school after reports of the attack emerged, Arsit Sampantharat, the permanent secretary of the interior ministry, told PPTV.A lockdown at the school was declared over in about half an hour.

articles.title: ‘Mamma mia!’: Trump tariffs refund ignites 53% profit spike at Nintendo
articles.excerpt: Nintendo has reported a jump in profits, as the Japanese game maker’s earnings were buoyed up by a long-awaited refund on Donald Trump’s tariffs.The company said profits surged 53.5% to ¥147.4bn (£694m) over the three months to June, substantially beating expert forecasts for ¥77.8bn.Nintendo said sales of its Switch 2 console, which was released last summer, “maintained strong sales momentum”, while popular games such as Yoshi and the Mysterious Book, Star Fox, and Pokémon Pokopia “performed steadily”. However, that did not make up for an overall drop in sales compared with the same period last year, with revenue down by 10% to ¥517.8bn.Instead, Nintendo said profits were aided by a refund on US tariffs, after the country’s supreme court ruled in February that Donald Trump’s sweeping “liberation day” trade levies were illegal.The Trump administration has refunded about $100bn from the tariffs charged before the court ruling, representing 60% of the total $165bn collected. Trump has continued to pitch tariffs as a solution for the US economy, bringing back domestic production, securing better trade deals and closing the deficit in the federal budget.Nintendo’s Tokyo-listed shares were up 2.87% on Thursday after the earnings release.The company filed a lawsuit weeks after the US supreme court ruling, demanding a full refund from the White House that would cover what it spent on tariffs, plus interest.While a refund now appears to have come through, Nintendo stopped short of confirming the full amount, at a time when it is still appears to be resisting calls to pass those refunds on to consumers.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotionLast month, Nintendo was hit with a class action lawsuit on behalf of customers, which claims the company hiked its prices because of tariffs but later benefited from the refunds.

articles.title: Australia news live: NSW schools may ban take-home tests over AI concerns; minister calls urgent meeting over airport chaos
articles.excerpt: From 1h agoNSW deputy premier asks for moratorium on take-home assessments for students amid AI reviewPrue Car, the NSW deputy premier, has asked the NSW Education Standards Authority (Nesa) to impose a ban on unsupervised take-home assessments during a broad review of AI’s impact on student learning.Car said she has asked Nesa to “urgently” examine artificial intelligence and move to protect student learning amid growing evidence the technology is affecting student’s cognitive development. Half of students’ HSC result is based on school-based assessments, some of which is finished outside the classroom.She said in a statement: double quotation markArtificial intelligence has enormous potential to support teaching and learning, but it should never replace the thinking, creativity, and hard work that education is designed to develop. The purpose of schooling extends beyond producing an assessment task. It is to build knowledge, judgment, resilience, and critical thinking over time. If students rely on AI to bypass that learning process, we risk undermining both their education and the integrity of the HSC.
articles.summary: 新南威尔士州副州长普吕·卡尔已要求新州教育标准局（Nesa）在对人工智能影响学生学习的广泛审查期间，禁止学生进行无监督的带回家评估。卡尔表示，她已要求Nesa“紧急”审查人工智能并采取行动保护学生学习，因为越来越多证据表明该技术正在影响学生的认知发展。学生高考HSC成绩的一半基于校内评估，其中部分在校外完成。她在声明中表示：“人工智能在支持教学方面潜力巨大，但绝不应取代教育旨在培养的思考、创造力和努力。学校教育的意义不仅限于完成评估任务，而是随着时间的推移构建知识、判断力、韧性和批判性思维。如果学生依赖人工智能绕过学习过程，我们可能既损害他们的教育，也损害HSC的公正性。”

articles.title: Body of woman found in suitcase by side of road in regional NSW
articles.excerpt: The body of a woman has been found in a suitcase by the side of a road south of Goulburn in regional New South Wales.NSW police said they were called to Wolgon Road, near Oallen Ford Road, at Oallen at about 12.50pm on Sunday “following reports a body had been located”.Officers travelled to the remote location and located the body in the suitcase.It was yet to be formally identified, a police spokesperson said on Sunday night.“Unfortunately, the female remains have been subject to a state of decomposition,” Supt Linda Bradbury told Channel 9 on Monday morning.“We’re conducting a number of enquiries to assist us in locating the identification of the female and also how she ended up in that location.“We are relying a lot on forensic evidence.”The discovery was made by two men who had pulled onto the side of the road by chance, Bradbury said.“They were able to tell us how they had come across it,” she added.“Unfortunately they were on a weekend drive, as a lot of people do over the weekend, and stopped for a break. [It was] quite a shocking discovery for them, absolutely.”A crime scene was established and the suitcase was “seized to undergo forensic examination while detectives commence an investigation into the incident”.Police did not immediately reveal how long the body may have been at the location.Oallen is in the southern tablelands region of NSW, about 109km north-east of Canberra and 225km south-west of Sydney.
articles.summary: 在新南威尔士州古尔本以南地区的一条路边，一名女性的尸体被发现装在手提箱内。新州警方表示，周日下午约12时50分接到“发现尸体”的报告后赶往奥伦附近的沃尔贡路。警员抵达该偏远地点后在手提箱内发现了这具尸体。警方发言人周日晚表示，尸体尚未正式确认身份。警司琳达·布拉德伯里周一上午对第九频道表示：“不幸的是，这具女性遗体已处于腐烂状态。我们正在进行多项调查，以协助确认这名女性的身份，以及她为何会出现在那个地点。我们很大程度上依赖法医证据。”布拉德伯里表示，发现尸体的是两名男子，他们偶然将车停在路边。她补充道：“他们向我们讲述了发现尸体的经过。不幸的是，他们像许多人在周末那样自驾出游，停下来休息，这对他们来说确实是个令人震惊的发现。”警方已设立犯罪现场，并“扣押手提箱进行法医检验，同时侦探已开始调查该事件”。警方未立即透露尸体可能在该地点停留了多长时间。奥伦位于新州南部高地地区，距堪培拉东北约109公里，悉尼西南约225公里。

articles.title: China expresses ‘grave concern’ as internal documents reveal suicide warning before death in Melbourne immigration detention
articles.excerpt: The US private prison company running Australia’s immigration detention system was warned that a newly detained Chinese citizen expressed suicidal ideation and had a history of self-harm less than 24 hours before she died by suicide in a Melbourne detention centre, internal documents show.The death has raised serious questions about whether the detainee was properly monitored and whether she was placed in an appropriate room, given her state of mind.It has also triggered an intervention from Australia’s biggest trading partner, Guardian Australia can reveal.The Chinese embassy has confirmed it has “lodged solemn representations and expressed grave concern to the Australian side” about the circumstances of the death.“China will closely follow the case and safeguard the safety and legitimate rights and interests of Chinese citizens,” an embassy spokesperson said.China’s public intervention creates a fresh headache for the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, who is already furious about a string of security lapses involving the government’s new immigration contractor, Secure Journeys, a local subsidiary of the US-based prison multinational Management and Training Corporation.In May the Guardian revealed that a series of failures had allowed the escape of high-risk detainees, caused ill-equipped staff to be stabbed and hospitalised and triggered multiple investigations, one of which warned that MTC’s “minimalist staffing model” was putting workers and detainees at risk.Burke took the extraordinary step of hauling in the global president of MTC for a face-to-face dressing down in September 2025, just six months after the company was awarded the $2.3bn onshore immigration detention contract.On 10 July Australian Border Force issued a short statement saying a detainee had been found dead in the Melbourne immigration detention centre that morning.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailThe detainee was a Chinese citizen in her mid-30s who had been picked up the day

articles.title: Sydney gardener fined almost $200,000 for removing 287 trees to improve harbourside mansion’s water views
articles.excerpt: It began with a gardener being hired to trim grass at a harbourside mansion in Sydney – and escalated to payments being left in a shoe for the unlawful felling of hundreds of native trees in protected bushland.Now a court has fined Yi Wang $187,500 for his role in organising and carrying out the destruction of 287 trees from council-owned foreshore bushland at Woodford Bay in Longueville in late 2023.The New South Wales land and environment court justice Rachel Pepper convicted Wang last week for helping to orchestrate the clearing of 1,210 sq metres of land beside a waterfront property on Lucretia Avenue.Wang pleaded guilty to three offences in relation to the unlawful clearing, which Pepper heard destroyed potential habitat for a range of protected and threatened animals, including powerful owls and microbats. It could take three decades to recover.The tree vandalism occurred on public land on the foreshore of Woodford Bay in Longueville. Photograph: supplied by Lane Cove councilThe unlawful tree clearing also greatly reduced the natural protection previously afforded to an Aboriginal midden, the court heard.When it sold in 2014 for $7.6m, real estate agents described the Lucretia Avenue property as an “exclusive waterfront” residence commanding “water views from every room”. It boasted a private beach and was “bordering lush reserves”.The director of Sydney Garden Home, Wang was hired by the stepdaughter of the owner of the adjacent property to the bushland, Yao Wu, for grass trimming work in November 2023.The next day, Wu asked Wang to clear trees as well, including on public land.“This is my back yard,” Wang would later claim Wu repeatedly told him.Wang then hired casual labourers, including a chainsaw operator, and chopped down and removed trees over a 12-day period.

articles.title: Labor open to ‘sensible amendments’ on gambling reforms, minister says – as it happened
articles.excerpt: From 18h agoWhat we learned, Sunday 9 AugustThanks for joining us today. We’re wrapping up the live news blog. Here’s a reminder of the top stories from today: Labor frontbencher Jenny McAllister says the government still thinks they’ve “broadly got the legislation right” on gambling reform but that they’re open to “sensible amendments” if some come forward; Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young has delivered an ultimatum to the Albanese government over its gambling reform, saying the party will not vote for the proposed legislation as it stands; Two planes have narrowly avoided a collision on the tarmac at Sydney airport this morning as it struggles with staff shortages; The premier of South Australia, Peter Malinauskas has visited Apple’s headquarters and met with outgoing chief executive Tim Cook in the United States. Victoria’s new premier, Ben Carroll, says the state government will boost its funding for public schools before the November election,opening up a pathway for a federal cash injection. New South Wales recorded its first cases of H5 bird flu in two local birds on Saturday, including one found near Wentworth on the Murray-Darling Basin.

articles.title: Labour seeking ‘deeper relationship’ with EU under Burnham, new minister says
articles.excerpt: The UK will move faster and be more ambitious on achieving closer ties with Europe under Andy Burnham’s government, his new chief post-Brexit negotiator has said.Hamish Falconer, the new cabinet minister in charge of the EU reset talks, said there was “room to be ambitious” within Labour’s red lines on Europe, which exclude reopening discussions on the single market and customs union, and he would look at the “art of the possible”.He said greater cooperation on services – which might include visa-free travel for British people working in the EU, or mutual recognition of qualifications – was the next big area where the UK hoped to make progress. “I would want a deeper relationship, a more ambitious relationship with the EU,” Falconer told the Guardian.“There’s also a whole range of areas in relation to services where I’d really like it to be progressed. Services is obviously an area where the EU itself is less closely integrated and there’s a lot of discussion within the EU about where to take the productivity challenge for them – that’s a challenge we can recognise here in the UK as well. So, particularly on services, I’m really interested in where we can go further.”Falconer, the son of the Labour grandee Charlie Falconer, is a former Middle East minister and diplomat who has experience as a Foreign Office negotiator. He said he wanted “a sense of renewed pace” in the talks – though there is still no new summit date in sight. The long-awaited reset summit, which had been proposed for July, was postponed after Keir Starmer resigned as prime minister in June.“We’re committed to our manifesto red lines, but all of my experiences as a negotiator and the art of the possible is in part shaped by the nature of the relationship between two people negotiating,” Falconer said.“I used to be a negotiator with the Taliban.

articles.title: Italy condemns Spain’s ‘unacceptable’ border controls as Ceuta fallout intensifies
articles.excerpt: Italy’s foreign minister has called Spain’s decision to impose retaliatory checks on travellers from Italy “incomprehensible and completely unacceptable” as people making their way between the two EU countries were left grappling with the effects of the escalating feud.Spain started carrying out spot checks on visitors from Italy at midnight on Saturday. The tit-for-tat move came after Rome infuriated Madrid by launching checks on 1 August for travellers from Spain in response to the recent influx of about 72,000 people into Ceuta, a Spanish territory in north Africa.Spanish officials were swift to point out that the Italian checks made little sense, given that by 1 August, the border in Ceuta was back under control and the vast majority of those who had arrived had been returned to Morocco. Ceuta is not part of the Schengen free-movement zone, Madrid has repeatedly stressed, meaning there is little chance of onward travel to continental Europe without EU citizenship or residency.The checks by Italy had led to “intolerable” scenes at Italian airports, Spain’s foreign minister, José Manuel Albares, told reporters. “This measure is, first and foremost, an attack on the dignity of the Spanish people, but, secondly, it is a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity,” he said.In an interview published on Sunday in La Stampa, Italy’s foreign minister defended the move by Rome. “Some order needs to be brought in: we’re not against Spain, but we have a duty to protect our borders,” said Antonio Tajani, voicing concerns about some of the migrants potentially holding jihadist views. “What is incomprehensible and completely unacceptable is Spain’s reaction.”He pushed back against the suggestion that Rome’s actions were symbolic, given the remote possibility of anyone making it to Italy from Ceuta. “Where do they go after arriving in Spain? Italy, as a destination, is the country most at risk.

articles.title: Russian family denied asylum in Finland fear reprisals for pro-Ukraine activism
articles.excerpt: A Russian family faces deportation from Finland after repeatedly being denied asylum – despite the threat of arrest, imprisonment and potential torture for their pro-Ukrainian activism.Nikita and Olga Belov fled their homeland in 2022 after attracting the attention of Russian authorities – including military summons, threatening messages and attempts to locate them – after expressing opposition to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.Nikita, 25, left his engineering job at a research institute in Moscow specialising in metallurgical technologies after finding out the work he was doing was connected to the Russian war effort.Since arriving in Finland on visas, Nikita and his mother, Olga, 55, a nurse anaesthetist, have been vocal supporters of Ukraine and public in their active support and coordination of aid sent to the country and its armed forces. But the Finnish immigration service told the mother and son that despite this they face “no real risk” if they return to Russia.In April, they were detained by Finnish authorities pending deportation. They were later released after a court intervention but are now awaiting a decision that could result in them being deported within weeks.Nikita Belov and his mother, Olga, are strong supporters of Ukraine and critics of Putin’s war. Photograph: Nikita BelovThe Belov case is understood to be one of many of Russians being denied asylum in neighbouring Finland where legal experts deem their future risk and human rights have not been sufficiently assessed.Between February 2022 and June 2026, the Finnish immigration service deported 1,039 Russians according to official statistics: the most of any nationality. During the same period, 1,109 of 1,342 Russians were refused entry to Finland in connection with a negative asylum application.Since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Finland’s relationship with its neighbour has shifted drastically.

articles.title: Navy says it is spending 25% more time monitoring Russian vessels around UK waters
articles.excerpt: The Royal Navy has warned of increasing Russian activity around the UK’s waters after it spent 21 days in July monitoring Moscow’s ships.Naval operations to monitor Russian vessels increased by 25% last month compared with the previous year, with warships making repeated voyages through the strait of Dover and the North Sea.Offshore patrol vessels HMS Tyne, HMS Mersey and HMS Severn, alongside Wildcat helicopters from 815 Naval Air Squadron and Merlin submarine-hunting aircraft, were deployed throughout the month to shadow Russian frigates Neustrashimy and Admiral Grigorovich, which are tasked with escorting so-called “shadow fleet” tankers.Last month, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in its annual report that Royal Navy vessels had been “activated” 116 times in the year to March 2026, shadowing 61 Russian warships and 28 merchant vessels around the UK’s waters.This reflected a 30% increase in Russian naval activity over the previous two years and included operations to deter the spy ship Yantar, which was spotted near undersea cables off Scotland last November.Vladimir Putin has been accused of using the Kremlin’s shadow fleet of ageing vessels to evade international sanctions on its oil and fund the war in Ukraine.The increase in Russian naval activity follows the seizure of the tanker Smyrtos by Royal Marines in June, the first time British troops have directly boarded a shadow fleet vessel.The MoD said the diversion of ships from Russia to escort shadow fleet vessels meant the country was “using up valuable operational capacity to constantly guard cargo”.The UK has already imposed sanctions on more than 500 vessels, and Russia’s oil and gas revenues fell by 24% year on year in 2025.HMS Tyne was also tasked with monitoring the Neustrashimy as it carried out a live-firing exercise outside British and French waters on 20 July.Another ship, the frigate HMS Somerset, has been involved in monitoring Russian activity in the North Atlantic as part of a four-month

articles.title: The Bond effect? How MI6 fascinates spy watchers around the world
articles.excerpt: MI6 has the swagger of James Bond; its French equivalent, DGSE, the complexities of the television drama Le Bureau. The film and TV shows may be fictional, but a survey run by a French magazine that placed the British spy agency above the French as No 1 across all of Europe this week is not.L’Express, a news weekly, conducted a Eurovision-style poll of 60 current and former spies from across the continent, plus the CIA and Israel’s Mossad. Each was asked to rank their top five foreign intelligence agencies, in secret, naturally enough. MI6 was first with 251 points ahead of DGSE on 169, with other agencies trailing behind.The result did not surprise Alexandra Saviana, a deputy editor at the publication, specialising in defence and intelligence, but the margin of victory did. “It is a huge point gap,” she said, reflecting the opinions of insiders and allies, 17 of whom are or were agency chiefs in a interconnected, covert ecosystem.At MI6’s headquarters in Vauxhall, London, there has been no sign of a public reaction from its chief, Blaise Metreweli. But there is a quiet satisfaction at the unexpected verdict, not least because the agency values how it is perceived by both allies and adversaries. “Reputation matters a lot in the espionage game,” said a former Whitehall insider.MI6’s headquarters in London. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images“British spies fascinate Europe, and beyond,” L’Express explained in its cover story.

articles.title: Netanyahu rejects US-led 15-point Gaza peace plan in rare public break with Trump
articles.excerpt: Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has rejected a US-backed 15-point peace plan for Gaza in a rare public break with Donald Trump.In a statement on Sunday, Netanyahu said that he was confronting a “wave of rumours about Israeli weakness and Israeli withdrawals on all fronts” and rebuked US pressure to end wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran without Israel’s buy-in.On Gaza, he said: “Israel does not accept the 15-point document. The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed. And when I say the disarming of Hamas, it means heavy weaponry, lighter weaponry, all weaponry. And we are talking about genuine disarmament, not fictitious disarmament. Right now, we are talking with the Americans about this issue.”Trump’s Board of Peace in July proposed the 15-point plan, which mandated that Hamas disarm in exchange for providing a full Israeli military withdrawal from the Gaza Strip and an eventual transition of power to an independent Palestinian National Committee. Trump had said that the agreement would be implemented in stages, but Netanyahu on Sunday said that he wanted a full disarmament first in order to implement the deal.Israeli attacks have continued on Gaza despite a ceasefire brokered last October. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty ImagesThe Israeli leader’s main target in his remarks was the US. Israel has emerged as a key stumbling block in the Trump White House’s plans to broker peace in the region, in Israel’s conflicts in Gaza and Lebanon as well as in the war begun by joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran. And Netanyahu, who is facing tough elections in October and pressure from hardliners in his own government, appears ready to test his relationship with Trump in public in order to shore up his reputation as a defender of Israel at home.Israel had already signalled that it would reject the US-led plan.

articles.title: Netanyahu rejects Trump’s Gaza plan and vows no withdrawal until Hamas disarms – as it happened
articles.excerpt: From 3h agoThe day so farWe’re wrapping our live coverage of the Middle East crisis for today. Here are Sunday’s top developments: Israel has rebuffed Donald Trump’s Gaza plan. The country said it would not leave Gaza unless Hamas was “genuinely” disarmed. Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that they were discussing their concerns with the US. “They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters,” Netanyahu said. Donald Trump said he’s “low keying it” with Iran as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Trump’s comments to Axios came after Iran said it would not agree to a deal until the US met its demands, which included never speaking insulting the country. “We are only semi-negotiating with them,” Trump also told Axios. Although Donald Trump has rebuffed claims that the US is running low on weapons crucial to its war on Iran, a leaked memo indicates that his military leadership is concerned by falling stockpiles. Per the Washington Post, deputy US defense secretary Steve Feinberg on Wednesday told defense industry leaders that they must “drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and/or increased production for critical capabilities.” Meanwhile, Trump’s war on Iran continues to draw prominent criticism in the US. New York’s Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said Trump’s complaints about rising costs clash with his policies that has made daily life more expensive. “Donald Trump may be saying that oil companies are making too much money, but what Donald Trump is doing is starting a reckless war in Iran, having closed door meetings with oil companies before his election, saying, you know, you give me money, you give me campaign contributions, and I will do whatever you want,” Ocasio-Cortez said on ABC.

articles.title: Iran-aligned Houthis claim they attacked oil refinery in Saudi Arabia
articles.excerpt: Yemen’s Tehran-aligned Houthis have claimed responsibility for an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, two days after the kingdom signed ⁠a defence pact with Turkey ⁠and Pakistan in response to ​growing regional instability caused by the US-Israel war on Iran.The attack early on Sunday came after Iran said tough new demands would have to be met before it would reopen the strait of Hormuz, and after the United Arab Emirates said one of its ships had been targeted by an Iranian missile, as a deal to open the waterway remained out of reach.Iran’s supreme national security council said the strait would not open until the US corrected its “behaviour”.The US must never threaten Iran again and permanently end the war with Tehran and its armed allies in the region, said the statement from the council’s secretary, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a former commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).He added that the US must also end the naval blockade of Iranian ports and withdraw its military from the area, “completely compensate” Iran for war damage, lift sanctions and “unconditionally” release frozen assets.There was no immediate comment from the US. According to the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by the US and Iran in June, a timetable to end sanctions and a plan for compensation would be part of a final peace deal, and negotiations would address frozen assets.The Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said on Saturday that Iran and Oman were close to reaching an agreement on navigation through the strait, “specifically the determination of a transit route”.But the waterway’s reopening was contingent on other conditions, Araghchi said, in remarks shared on social media. He blamed the situation on what he called the US violation of the June MoU.Oman, which is mediating and has made relatively few comments on the Hormuz talks, said on Saturday that the discussions were continuing “in a positive and constructive atmosphere”.

articles.title: Iran issues tough demands to reopen strait of Hormuz as deal still out of reach
articles.excerpt: Iran has issued tough new demands for reopening the strait of Hormuz, while the United Arab Emirates said one of its ships was targeted by an Iranian missile, as a deal to open the strategic waterway remained out of reach on Saturday.Iran’s politburo-like body known as the supreme national security council said the strait of Hormuz will not open until the United States “corrects its behaviour”, and its state broadcaster published a statement from the council’s secretary, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who is also a commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).The US must never threaten Iran again, the statement said, and must permanently end the war with Iran and its armed allies in the region. The US must lift the naval blockade of Iranian ports and withdraw its military from the area. It also must “completely compensate” Iran for war damage, lift sanctions and “unconditionally” release frozen assets.There was no immediate comment from the US, which has wanted an acceptable deal on the strait before ending the blockade. According to the interim deal signed in June, a schedule to end sanctions and a plan for compensation would be part of the final deal, and negotiations would address frozen assets.The Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said on Saturday that they were close to reaching an agreement on navigation, “specifically the determination of a transit route”.

articles.title: Demi Vollering wins Tour de France for the 2nd time
articles.excerpt: Netherlands' Demi Vollering celebrates on the podium after winning the Women's Tour de France cycling race in Nice, France, Sunday, Aug. 9, 2026. Philippe Magoni/AP hide caption toggle caption Philippe Magoni/AP After winning the Women's Tour de France for the second time on Sunday, Demi Vollering tried hard to hold back tears while the Dutch national anthem played. It was her toughest moment of the day after an ultra-dominant performance on the bike from the 2023 champion. She secured an impressive stage win, and in doing so extended her overall lead over Polish rider Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney to 1 minute, 18 seconds clear of the 2024 champion. Vollering raised her bike in the air moments after crossing the finish line in Nice. Niewiadoma-Phinney had started Sunday's ninth and final stage only eight seconds behind Vollering, who got a time bonus for winning it. Finally, as the Dutch anthem ended, a lone tear trickled down the side of Vollering's face. A few more soon followed as her achievement hit home. "It's not only the dream of winning the Tour de France. It's also the dream of living this life, of working hard along with passionate people," the 29-year-old Vollering said. "It all starts with dreaming. Go chase the dreams and don't let anyone stop you." Nobody could on Sunday. Knowing that she was well clear, Vollering began to celebrate as the line approached, raising her arm in triumph and then tapping her head with her finger to show her mental strength. "I was thinking about a lot of things as I was approaching the finish line. I thought that I had never won in the yellow jersey before," Vollering said. "I thought about how much work has gone into this victory. I thought about the people who have been behind me." She finished the stage 1 minute, 4 seconds ahead of Spaniard Paula Blasi Cairol and Niewiadoma-Phinney, who looked tired but was all smiles later on the podium.
articles.summary: 荷兰选手德米·沃勒林在周日第二次赢得女子环法自行车赛冠军，她在荷兰国歌奏响时努力忍住泪水。这是她当天最艰难的时刻，此前她在自行车上展现了超强的统治力。这位2023年的冠军获得了令人瞩目的赛段胜利，并将对波兰选手卡塔日娜·涅维亚多马-菲尼的总领先优势扩大到1分18秒，领先这位2024年冠军。在尼斯冲过终点线后，沃勒林将自行车举向空中。涅维亚多马-菲尼在周日第九赛段（也是最终赛段）开始前仅落后沃勒林8秒，而沃勒林因获胜获得了时间奖励。最终，当荷兰国歌结束，一滴泪水沿着沃勒林的脸颊滑落，随后更多的泪水涌出，她的成就终于让她感到震撼。这位29岁的沃勒林表示：「这不仅仅是赢得环法自行车赛的梦想，也是体验这种生活、与热情的人一起努力工作的梦想。一切始于梦想，去追逐梦想，不要被任何人阻止。」周日，没有人能阻止她。知道自己遥遥领先，沃勒林在接近终点时开始庆祝，举起手臂庆祝胜利，然后用手指敲了敲头，展示她的精神力量。她说：「冲过终点线时，我想到很多事情。我想到自己从未穿着黄色领骑衫获胜，想到为这场胜利付出的努力，想到支持我的人们。」她以领先西班牙选手保拉·布拉斯·凯罗尔和涅维亚多马-菲尼1分4秒的成绩完成赛段，涅维亚多马-菲尼虽然看起来很疲惫，但在领奖台上笑容满面。
